title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Hormuz is still shut in practice: an ADNOC L&S vessel was hit on Tuesday night, and a US Navy official told the Senate one transit now costs $64m to insure. On land the picture is steadier, with DP World moving east-coast cargo by road and rail and UAE fuel prices set to ease.

stories.headline: $64m to insure one Hormuz transit, US Navy official tells Senate
body: Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao told a Senate hearing on Tuesday that insurance for one Hormuz transit now costs $64m. He said the pre-war cost was $54,000. Al Jazeera notes the figure has not been independently verified.
UKMTO puts traffic about 65% below pre-war levels, with 308 crossings in the week to 11 November. Iran says ships must use approved routes and has exempted vessels from India, China, Iraq and Qatar.
stories.soWhat: Even if the number is high, the direction is clear. War-risk costs on Gulf-bound sea freight are not coming down this month.

stories.headline: ADNOC L&S vessel hit in the strait; one missing, 11 injured
body: An ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening. Gulf News reports one crew member missing and 11 injured. Straits Daily Brief says the LPG carrier Tara Gas is now on fire and adrift.
The US has widened its maritime blockade. CENTCOM warned that ships taking cargo at sea from Iran-loaded vessels could face action. Ships holding position in the Gulf rose to 43.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: a UAE-flagged operator is now among the casualties. Expect owners to cut Gulf sailings further and east-coast ports to stay crowded.

stories.headline: DP World speeds up Dh2.5bn Fujairah ports; 1 million TEU moved by land
body: DP World now expects its two new Fujairah-area ports, Al Rugaylat and Dibba, to start phased operations in 18 to 24 months, down from 24 to 30. From March to October it moved more than 1 million TEU from east-coast ports to Jebel Ali by truck and rail, about 3,500 TEU a day.
Jebel Ali stayed open throughout, with only six hours of total disruption. DP World expects volumes to return one to three months after safe passage through Hormuz is restored.
stories.soWhat: The east-coast-to-Jebel Ali land bridge is now a permanent part of UAE logistics. Our trucking and customs offer should be built around it.

stories.headline: Drone threats spread to Bahrain and Kuwait; more airlines cut Saudi flights
body: Bahrain intercepted Iranian attacks early on Wednesday, and Kuwait reported hostile drone threats. Air Arabia cancelled Sharjah–Riyadh and Sharjah–Abha flights on 18 November.
IndiGo has suspended Riyadh and Dammam to 30 November, and Akasa Air Riyadh and Jeddah to the same date. Etihad's Riyadh and Dammam cargo cancellations to 30 November stand.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: more carriers are pulling Saudi capacity, and Kuwait is now on the threat map. Belly space into Saudi stays scarce.

stories.headline: UAE fuel could fall again in December
body: November pump prices were cut by Dh0.24 a litre, with Super 98 at Dh4.16. Brent averaged $96.91 in the first two weeks of November, against $123.57 in the same weeks of October.
UAE prices follow global prices with a one-month lag, so a second cut in December is possible.
stories.soWhat: Lower fuel eases last-mile cost. Check our domestic fuel surcharge tracks the index down as well as up.

stories.headline: Dubai Taxi's delivery-bike fleet passes 4,000
body: Dubai Taxi Company says its delivery-bike fleet passed 4,000 bikes by September, up 77% on last year, and made over 900,000 deliveries that month. Q2 delivery-bike revenue rose 53% to AED 27.9 million.
Its partners include Talabat, Careem, Deliveroo, noon and Keeta. UAE restaurant delivery orders rose 15% in H1 2026. Figures are from an opinion piece by DTC's CEO.
stories.soWhat: Rider capacity in Dubai is being built by fleet operators. That is a partner option for our peak last-mile, and a competitor for platform contracts.

competitors.name: DP World
competitors.headline: Egypt-to-UAE fresh produce corridor with Majid Al Futtaim; autonomous trucks at Jebel Ali
body: DP World and Majid Al Futtaim signed an MoU on 16 November to raise Egyptian exports to the UAE. Fresh produce will be consolidated in cold stores at Sokhna, shipped on DP World feeders and trucked chilled to Jebel Ali for MAF's stores.

On 15 November Dubai Future Foundation named DP World first strategic partner of SHIFFT, a self-driving logistics venture with Oxa. Work starts at Jebel Ali, where DP World runs more than 900 vehicles.
competitors.soWhat: DP World is selling end-to-end cold chain direct to big retailers. We should defend our grocery and retail accounts with a combined freight, customs and cold-chain offer.
competitors.source: Logistics Update Africa; Robotics & Automation News

competitors.name: Amazon
competitors.headline: New 196,000 sq ft Dubai office; more than 3,000 UAE staff
body: Sheikh Hamdan visited Amazon's new office in Dubai Internet City on 17 November. Amazon says it has more than 3,000 employees in the UAE. It also showed Alexa for Shopping, now in beta for UAE customers.
competitors.soWhat: Amazon keeps investing in the UAE. Its own delivery network grows with it, so third-party volume from Amazon is not something to plan on.

competitors.name: DHL Global Forwarding
competitors.headline: Building up near Khor Fakkan, Dibba and Fujairah
body: DHL Global Forwarding's Middle East and Africa CEO Tobias Maier says the unit will strengthen its position near Khor Fakkan, Dibba and Fujairah. DHL's €500 million Gulf commitment is unchanged, and it has a 20-year joint venture with Etihad Rail.
Maier expects logistics to normalise three to six months after the conflict ends.
competitors.soWhat: DHL is moving to the same east-coast bypass we sell. We need to lock in east-coast customers before its capacity lands.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: CEO: freight rates may take 6–12 months to ease after peace
body: Group CEO Amadou Diallo expects freight rates to normalise six to 12 months after peace returns. Aramex targets double-digit revenue growth in 2026 and 2027. Q3 revenue was a record Dh1.98 billion, still our latest figure.
On 3 November Aramex launched Data Center Logistics across the GCC, Southeast Asia, Taiwan and the southern US.
competitors.soWhat: Our own view is that high rates last well past any ceasefire. Pricing should assume that too, and DHL's 3–6 month view gives us room to argue it with customers.

opportunities.title: East-coast land bridge
opportunities.text: DP World moves about 3,500 TEU a day by land from the east coast. Sell our trucking and customs as the door-to-door layer on top.

opportunities.title: Egypt–UAE perishables
opportunities.text: The DP World–MAF corridor shows demand for chilled Egypt-to-UAE flows. Pitch our cold chain to other grocers and importers.

opportunities.title: Saudi road while air is cut
opportunities.text: IndiGo, Akasa, Air Arabia and Etihad have all pulled Saudi flights. Road UAE–Saudi remains the dependable option.

opportunities.title: Cheaper last-mile fuel
opportunities.text: A possible second fuel cut in December lowers domestic cost. Use it to win e-commerce volume, not just to widen margin.

opportunities.title: Data centre logistics
opportunities.text: Our new Data Center Logistics service fits the Gulf AI build-out. Target project owners while air capacity is tight.

watchouts.title: Insurance spike
watchouts.text: A $64m per-transit insurance claim, even unverified, will harden war-risk pricing. Sea surcharges stay high.

watchouts.title: UAE vessel hit
watchouts.text: The attack on an ADNOC L&S ship puts UAE-linked ships in the line of fire. Expect fewer feeder sailings into the Gulf.

watchouts.title: Kuwait and Bahrain
watchouts.text: Drone threats now reach Kuwait as well as Bahrain. Air and road services there may face sudden stops.

watchouts.title: DHL on the east coast
watchouts.text: DHL is building near Khor Fakkan, Dibba and Fujairah. Our east-coast edge may narrow within months.

watchouts.title: Surcharge credibility
watchouts.text: If fuel falls and we do not pass it through, customers will push back on war-risk surcharges too.

moves.title: Hold sea war-risk pass-through
moves.text: Keep current war-risk surcharges on Gulf sea quotes after the $64m insurance claim and the ADNOC L&S attack.

moves.title: Package an east-coast door-to-door product
moves.text: Combine Khor Fakkan/Fujairah handling, trucking to Jebel Ali and customs into one priced product, before DHL's build-up lands.

moves.title: Cold-chain pitch to grocers
moves.text: Use the DP World–MAF deal as the hook. Offer chilled Egypt and India import flows to other grocers and food importers.

moves.title: Index the domestic fuel surcharge down
moves.text: Prepare the December fuel surcharge cut now so it lands with the pump price change.

moves.title: Update Kuwait and Bahrain advisories
moves.text: Add Kuwait to the customer service notes next to Bahrain and Saudi air cuts.

moves.title: Push Saudi road to air-dependent shippers
moves.text: List IndiGo, Akasa, Air Arabia and Etihad Saudi cuts and offer road capacity to customers who rely on belly space.
